title: Field-level consistency watch for structured outputs
creator: Elena Gupta
description: We need a lightweight, field-level monitoring layer that can detect quality regressions in structured (JSON) outputs that are specifically correlated with configuration or model changes. Current structured-output checks operate at the whole-payload level and often miss subtle regressions like a field flip from integer to string, enum set shrinkage, or a spike in missingness for a rarely emitted field. This ticket delivers a watch that computes per-field signatures (type distribution, missing rate, common enum values, string length distribution) and emits deltas and alerts when a config/model change exceeds configurable thresholds. The watch will be integrated into rollout flows so engineers can see which fields regressed when a rollout completes or when we change runtime config (batching/quantization/kv-cache modes).
acceptance_criteria: Per-field signatures are computed for production baseline and candidate run samples (type histogram, missing rate, top-10 enum values, median + p90 string length).

Alerts are raised when any field exceeds its configured drift threshold (type-change, missing-rate delta > X%, JS divergence > Y) and include attribution to the config/model delta that triggered the evaluation.
A console dashboard shows field-level diffs and a ranked list of highest-impact fields for the last 30d and for the most recent rollout.
The watch is wired into canary rollouts: if a high-severity field regression is detected during a canary, the rollout can be automatically paused and a notification sent to the owners.
False positive rate on held-out synthetic tests remains below the agreed bar (see test_plan).
design_notes: Signature model: per-field vector with (type_histogram, missing_rate, enum_topk, length_quantiles). Use JS divergence for histograms and absolute delta for missing_rate.
Weight field deltas by field production frequency and by downstream eval importance (weigh fields used by golden evals higher).
Handle schema evolution: provide 'allowed growth' config per-field so new optional fields don't trigger warnings. Maintain a whitelist of intentionally evolving fields tied to PRs or feature flags.
Sampling: use production traces sampled at 0.5% by default but allow heavier sampling for candidate runs. Use stratified sampling across routes/tenants to avoid noisy single-tenant spikes.
Attribution: capture the exact config delta (git diff of rollout config + model version) that precedes the evaluation and include it in alert payload.
implementation_plan: 1) Extend eval-worker to compute per-field signatures as part of the existing structured-output eval pipeline (add module field_signatures).
2) Persist baseline signatures in a new table 'field_signatures_v1' keyed by model+config fingerprint+route. Store summary metrics, not raw samples.

3) Add an evaluation job that runs automatically after: a) model version change, b) runtime config change, c) scheduled daily baseline compare. Job computes deltas and writes findings to the alerts service.

4) Integrate with rollout service: after canary batch finishes, trigger the evaluation job and surface results in the rollout UI. If severity >= P0 threshold, mark rollout as paused and attach findings.
5) Build Console views: per-rollout field-diff table, field detail view with sample examples, and time-series for missing_rate and type distribution.
6) Add config for per-field thresholds and global sensitivity in the console and as YAML in rollout specs.
7) Add unit tests, synthetic regression harness, and a CI job that runs a known-regression sentinel to catch implementation regressions.
test_plan: Unit tests for signature calculator (type histograms, missing rate, enum extraction).
Synthetic injection tests: run eval pipeline with crafted datasets that induce known regressions (type flip, missing_rate spike, enum shrink) and verify alerts fire with correct field attribution.
Canary end-to-end: deploy a candidate model to a 1% canary route with injected regression and ensure rollout is paused automatically and owners are notified.
False-positive sweep: use a corpus of 100 recent rollouts with no known regressions to measure noise; tune thresholds until false positives < 3% for P1 alerts.
Load test: run signature aggregation on a 10k-sample batch within 5 minutes to ensure evaluation latency fits rollout windows.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): land schema + eval worker changes behind feature flag. Run internal synthetics and smoke tests (1 sprint).
Phase 2 (canary): enable watch for a small set of non-critical routes (0.5% traffic) for 2 weeks, collect telemetry and tune thresholds.
Phase 3 (gradual): enable for all rollouts but default sensitivity low; provide 'strict' mode toggle for teams requiring aggressive enforcement.

Mitigation: on high-severity detected during canary, automatically pause rollout and create a ticket with the field diff snapshot + sample examples. Manual rollback or model fallback will be performed by SRE if owners don't respond within SLA.
Communication: announce to platform-users channel and publish runbook for investigating field regressions (links below).
